newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to push privatisation despite problems.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to push privatisation despite problems.

text.p: The head of Bangladesh's privatisation board said on Sunday that the government would press ahead with its privatisation programme despite bureaucratic red tape and labour protests.
"I assure all of you that this process will continue," Kazi Zafarullah told members of the Economic Reporters Forum.
He said the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was determined to pursue the privatisation process as it would have positive and far-reaching socio-economic effects.
"Privatisation and private sector development is a difficult job. It becomes difficult due to inappropriate policies, coupled with lack of skills and the absence of enabling laws," he said.
In the past four years only 12 industries had been privatised, Zafarullah added.
He said the government had only taken decisions on privatising 17 state enterprises, against a target of 61, for the July 1996-June 1997 fiscal year.
Eight were ready to be handed over to new owners, and shares in the other nine would be floated on the stock exchange.

Zafarullah said the government was finalising a leagal framework to accelerate the privatisation process. It had identified 219 target companies, of which 82 would be transferred to private hands this year.
Organised labour was opposed to privatisation but workers were being assured that only surplus jobs would be cut, he said.
Red tape was another obstacle. "Civil servants in the corporations managing the state-owned companies are against privatisation because of their selfish interest," he said.
Zafarullah said parliamentarians from both ruling and opposition parties would be given a role in the board to speed up privatisation.
